questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A multinational financial enterprise operates 350 AWS accounts structured within AWS Organizations across multiple nested Organizational Units (OUs). The global security compliance office mandates that member account administrators and root users must be strictly prevented from creating unencrypted Amazon S3 buckets or disabling regional AWS CloudTrail trails. Concurrently, CI/CD automated deployment pipelines residing in the dedicated Shared-Services OU must retain full administrative privileges to provision and rotate AWS KMS customer managed keys (CMKs) without interruption. Which architecture enforces these security guardrails across the organization with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Deploy IAM Permission Boundaries across all existing and newly created IAM roles in all 350 accounts using AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks, adding explicit deny statements for unencrypted S3 actions and CloudTrail deletion while allowing KMS actions in Shared-Services pipelines.
options.explanation: Incorrect: IAM Permission Boundaries do not restrict the member account root user, do not apply to IAM service-linked roles automatically, and require extensive administrative maintenance across 350 accounts compared to centralized organization policies.

options.text: Attach a Service Control Policy (SCP) to the Root container of AWS Organizations with explicit Deny statements for unencrypted S3 bucket creation and CloudTrail modification, and move the Shared-Services OU outside the Root container hierarchy to isolate its KMS operations.
options.explanation: Incorrect: In AWS Organizations, all Organizational Units and member accounts must reside under the Root container; an OU cannot be placed outside the Root container hierarchy.

options.text: Attach Service Control Policies (SCPs) with explicit Deny conditions at the intermediate OU levels for unencrypted S3 bucket creation and CloudTrail tampering, while applying a dedicated SCP to the Shared-Services OU that leaves KMS management actions unconstrained.
options.explanation: Correct: Service Control Policies (SCPs) applied at OU levels enforce preventive guardrails that apply to all principals (including the root user) within member accounts without affecting sibling OUs or requiring per-account IAM maintenance.

options.text: Deploy AWS CloudFormation StackSets to all member accounts to create AWS Config detective rules that trigger AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks to terminate non-compliant S3 buckets and restart stopped CloudTrail trails.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Config is a detective mechanism that acts after resources are created, failing the mandatory requirement to strictly prevent the creation of non-compliant resources at the API level.

questions.generalExplanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations enforce guardrails across member accounts and apply to all principals including the root user. Applying granular SCPs at intermediate OU levels protects accounts without disrupting specific administrative privileges needed in dedicated OUs.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Projetar Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Uma instituição financeira multinacional opera 350 contas AWS estruturadas no AWS Organizations em múltiplas Unidades Organizacionais (OUs) aninhadas. A equipe de conformidade de segurança exige que administradores e o usuário root de contas-membro sejam estritamente impedidos de criar buckets do Amazon S3 não criptografados ou desativar trilhas regionais do AWS CloudTrail. Simultaneamente, pipelines automatizados de CI/CD na OU de Serviços Compartilhados devem manter privilégios administrativos completos para provisionar e rotacionar chaves gerenciadas pelo cliente (CMKs) no AWS KMS sem interrupções. Qual arquitetura impõe esses guardrails de segurança na organização com a MENOR sobrecarga operacional?

options.text: Implantar IAM Permission Boundaries em todas as roles existentes e futuras em todas as 350 contas usando runbooks do AWS Systems Manager Automation, inserindo negações para ações de S3 sem criptografia e deleção do CloudTrail, liberando ações de KMS para pipelines na OU de Serviços Compartilhados.
options.explanation: Incorreto: As Permission Boundaries do IAM não restringem o usuário root das contas-membro, não cobrem automaticamente service-linked roles e exigem manutenção contínua complexa em 350 contas quando comparadas a políticas centralizadas de organização.

options.text: Anexar uma Service Control Policy (SCP) ao contêiner Raiz do AWS Organizations com declarações de Deny explícitas para criação de S3 não criptografado e modificação do CloudTrail, movendo a OU de Serviços Compartilhados para fora da hierarquia Raiz para isolar suas operações KMS.
options.explanation: Incorreto: No AWS Organizations, todas as Unidades Organizacionais e contas-membro devem residir obrigatoriamente sob o contêiner Raiz (Root); uma OU não pode ser posicionada fora da hierarquia Raiz.

options.text: Anexar Service Control Policies (SCPs) com condições de Deny explícitas nos níveis intermediários de OU para criação de buckets S3 não criptografados e adulteração do CloudTrail, aplicando uma SCP dedicada à OU de Serviços Compartilhados que mantém as ações de gerenciamento de KMS irrestritas.
options.explanation: Correto: As SCPs aplicadas nos níveis de OU impõem guardrails preventivos que se aplicam a todos os principais (inclusive o usuário root) dentro das contas-membro, sem impactar OUs irmãs e sem exigir manutenção individual de IAM em cada conta.

options.text: Implantar AWS CloudFormation StackSets em todas as contas-membro para criar regras detectivas no AWS Config que acionam runbooks do AWS Systems Manager Automation para excluir buckets S3 não conformes e reiniciar trilhas do CloudTrail interrompidas.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O AWS Config é uma ferramenta detectiva que atua após o recurso ser criado, violando a exigência mandatória de impedir preventivamente a criação de recursos fora de conformidade na camada de API.

pt.generalExplanation: As Service Control Policies (SCPs) no AWS Organizations são o mecanismo nativo ideal para aplicar limites de proteção (guardrails) preventivos em escala enterprise. A aplicação granular de SCPs em OUs intermediárias assegura que os controles afetem todos os usuários (incluindo root) sem prejudicar pipelines em OUs específicas.

es.domainName: Dominio 1: Diseñar Soluciones para la Complejidad Organizacional
es.statement: Una empresa financiera multinacional opera 350 cuentas de AWS estructuradas en AWS Organizations en múltiples Unidades Organizativas (OUs) anidadas. El equipo de seguridad y cumplimiento exige que los administradores de cuentas miembro y usuarios root tengan estrictamente prohibido crear buckets de Amazon S3 sin cifrar o desactivar seguimientos regionales de AWS CloudTrail. Al mismo tiempo, los canales automatizados de CI/CD en la OU de Servicios Compartidos deben conservar privilegios administrativos completos para aprovisionar y rotar claves administradas por el cliente (CMKs) en AWS KMS sin interrupciones. ¿Qué arquitectura impone estas barreras de seguridad en la organización con la MENOR sobrecarga operativa?

options.text: Implementar Límites de Permisos de IAM (Permission Boundaries) en todos los roles existentes y nuevos en las 350 cuentas mediante runbooks de AWS Systems Manager Automation, agregando denegaciones para S3 sin cifrar y eliminación de CloudTrail, permitiendo acciones de KMS en Servicios Compartidos.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Los límites de permisos de IAM no restringen al usuario root de las cuentas miembro, no se aplican automáticamente a roles vinculados al servicio y requieren un mantenimiento administrativo masivo en 350 cuentas en comparación con las políticas centralizadas.

options.text: Adjuntar una Service Control Policy (SCP) al contenedor Raíz de AWS Organizations con declaraciones de Deny explícitas para S3 no cifrado y modificación de CloudTrail, y mover la OU de Servicios Compartidos fuera de la jerarquía Raíz para aislar sus operaciones de KMS.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: En AWS Organizations, todas las Unidades Organizativas y cuentas miembro deben residir bajo el contenedor Raíz; una OU no se puede colocar fuera de la jerarquía del contenedor Raíz.

options.text: Adjuntar Service Control Policies (SCPs) con condiciones de Deny explícitas en los niveles intermedios de OU para la creación de S3 no cifrado y la manipulación de CloudTrail, aplicando una SCP dedicada a la OU de Servicios Compartidos que deja sin restricciones las acciones de KMS.
options.explanation: Correcto: Las SCPs aplicadas en niveles de OU imponen barreras preventivas que se aplican a todos los principales (incluido el usuario root) dentro de las cuentas miembro sin afectar a las OUs hermanas ni requerir mantenimiento de IAM por cuenta.

options.text: Implementar AWS CloudFormation StackSets en todas las cuentas miembro para crear reglas detectivas de AWS Config que activen runbooks de AWS Systems Manager Automation para eliminar buckets S3 no conformes y reiniciar CloudTrail detenido.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: AWS Config es un mecanismo detectivesco que actúa después de que se crean los recursos, fallando el requisito obligatorio de prevenir estrictamente la creación de recursos no conformes a nivel de API.

es.generalExplanation: Las Service Control Policies (SCPs) en AWS Organizations son el mecanismo fundamental para hacer cumplir las barreras preventivas en estructuras multicuenta, bloqueando acciones no autorizadas a nivel de API para todos los usuarios, incluido el root de la cuenta miembro.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: An enterprise connects 80 application VPCs across multiple AWS accounts to an AWS Transit Gateway in us-east-1. The corporate security policy dictates that all inter-VPC (east-west) and internet outbound (north-south) network traffic must be centrally inspected by stateful firewall appliances residing in a dedicated Central Inspection VPC. During initial traffic validation, network engineers observe that stateful TCP connections between VPCs in different Availability Zones are intermittently dropped due to asymmetric packet routing. Which solution resolves this routing issue while maintaining high availability and centralized security inspection?

options.text: Enable Transit Gateway Appliance Mode on the VPC attachment connecting the Central Inspection VPC to the AWS Transit Gateway across all configured Availability Zones.
options.explanation: Correct: Enabling Appliance Mode on the Transit Gateway attachment for the Inspection VPC ensures that bidirectional traffic between spokes and the inspection VPC flows through the same Availability Zone and firewall ENI, eliminating asymmetric drops.

options.text: Enable Equal-Cost Multi-Path (ECMP) routing on all Transit Gateway route tables and configure Source NAT (SNAT) on the egress NAT Gateways in each spoke application VPC.
options.explanation: Incorrect: ECMP operates at BGP/VPN layers and does not enforce Availability Zone symmetry for inter-VPC Transit Gateway attachments, and configuring SNAT in spoke VPCs bypasses centralized inspection visibility.

options.text: Establish bidirectional VPC Peering connections between all 80 application VPCs and deploy AWS Network Firewall endpoints directly within private subnets in every individual spoke VPC.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Full-mesh VPC Peering across 80 accounts creates severe management complexity (3,160 peering connections) and deploying firewall endpoints in each spoke multiplies licensing and operational overhead.

options.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer in each spoke VPC and configure path-based routing rules that forward all inter-VPC traffic to a Network Load Balancer in the Central Inspection VPC.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Application Load Balancers operate exclusively at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and cannot inspect or route arbitrary Layer 3 and Layer 4 TCP/UDP network flows across enterprise VPCs.

questions.generalExplanation: Enabling Transit Gateway Appliance Mode on the Inspection VPC attachment forces bidirectional traffic for a given session to be processed by the same Availability Zone and ENI, ensuring stateful firewalls maintain TCP connection state.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Projetar Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Uma empresa interconecta 80 VPCs de aplicação em múltiplas contas AWS a um AWS Transit Gateway em us-east-1. A política de segurança corporativa determina que todo o tráfego entre VPCs (leste-oeste) e de saída para a internet (norte-sul) seja inspecionado centralmente por appliances de firewall com estado em uma VPC de Inspeção Central dedicada. Durante os testes iniciais, engenheiros de rede observam que conexões TCP com estado entre VPCs em diferentes Zonas de Disponibilidade caem intermitentemente devido ao roteamento assimétrico de pacotes. Qual solução resolve esse problema mantendo alta disponibilidade e inspeção centralizada?

options.text: Habilitar o recurso Transit Gateway Appliance Mode no anexo de VPC que conecta a VPC de Inspeção Central ao AWS Transit Gateway em todas as Zonas de Disponibilidade configuradas.
options.explanation: Correto: A ativação do Appliance Mode no anexo do Transit Gateway para a VPC de Inspeção garante que o fluxo bidirecional passe pela mesma Zona de Disponibilidade e ENI de firewall, eliminando descarte por assimetria.

options.text: Habilitar o roteamento Equal-Cost Multi-Path (ECMP) em todas as tabelas de rotas do Transit Gateway e configurar Source NAT (SNAT) nos NAT Gateways em cada VPC spoke de aplicação.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O ECMP atua em camadas BGP/VPN e não garante a simetria de Zona de Disponibilidade em anexos de VPC do Transit Gateway, além de que usar SNAT nas spokes prejudica a visibilidade centralizada de IP de origem.

options.text: Estabelecer conexões de VPC Peering bidirecionais entre todas as 80 VPCs de aplicação e implantar endpoints do AWS Network Firewall diretamente em sub-redes privadas de cada VPC spoke individual.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Uma malha completa de VPC Peering em 80 contas gera complexidade extrema de gestão (3.160 conexões de peering) e provisionar endpoints de firewall em cada spoke multiplica drasticamente custos e sobrecarga operacional.

options.text: Implantar um Application Load Balancer em cada VPC spoke e configurar regras de roteamento baseadas em caminho para encaminhar todo o tráfego entre VPCs a um Network Load Balancer na VPC de Inspeção Central.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Application Load Balancers operam exclusivamente na Camada 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) e não conseguem inspecionar ou rotear fluxos genéricos de rede de Camada 3 e Camada 4 (TCP/UDP) entre VPCs corporativas.

pt.generalExplanation: A habilitação do Appliance Mode no anexo de VPC da VPC de Inspeção no Transit Gateway força o tráfego bidirecional de uma sessão a passar pela mesma Zona de Disponibilidade e interface ENI, garantindo que firewalls stateful mantenham o estado da conexão TCP.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A technology conglomerate has 120 development accounts managed under AWS Organizations in the same AWS Region. The network engineering team mandates that all subnets, route tables, IPv4 CIDR allocations, and egress NAT Gateways must be centrally owned and managed in a dedicated Network Hub account. However, development teams in member accounts must be able to deploy Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon ECS tasks, and Amazon RDS databases into these centrally managed subnets without gaining permissions to modify network topologies or routing. Which solution satisfies these architectural requirements with the LEAST operational complexity and cost?

options.text: Deploy an AWS Transit Gateway in the Network Hub account, provision individual VPCs in each of the 120 member accounts, and create VPC attachments and route table associations for every member account.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Creating and managing 120 individual VPCs multiplies CIDR management complexity, Transit Gateway attachment fees ($0.05/hour per attachment), and redundant NAT Gateway infrastructure costs.

options.text: Configure a centralized multi-tier VPC in the Network Hub account and use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the private subnets with the entire organization or specific developer OUs.
options.explanation: Correct: VPC Sharing via AWS RAM allows central network administrators to retain complete control over VPC infrastructure while member accounts seamlessly launch compute and database resources directly in shared subnets.

options.text: Establish full-mesh VPC Peering connections between the Network Hub VPC and all 120 member account VPCs, creating scheduled Lambda functions to synchronize route table entries dynamically.
options.explanation: Incorrect: VPC Peering requires separate VPCs in each account, does not allow sharing subnets directly, and custom Lambda routing synchronization introduces significant operational failure risk.

options.text: Deploy AWS PrivateLink endpoint services in the Network Hub account for each application component and create Interface VPC Endpoints inside every development member account VPC.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS PrivateLink is designed for exposing specific TCP service endpoints, not for sharing generic multi-tier subnets where applications can deploy arbitrary compute and database resources.

questions.generalExplanation: VPC Sharing via AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) allows the central network account to share subnets with member accounts in the organization, enabling developers to launch resources directly without managing network infrastructure.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Projetar Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Um conglomerado de tecnologia possui 120 contas de desenvolvimento gerenciadas no AWS Organizations na mesma Região AWS. A equipe de engenharia de rede exige que todas as sub-redes, tabelas de rotas, alocações de blocos CIDR IPv4 e NAT Gateways de saída sejam centralmente pertencentes e gerenciados em uma conta de Hub de Rede dedicada. No entanto, as equipes de desenvolvimento nas contas-membro devem ser capazes de implantar instâncias Amazon EC2, tarefas Amazon ECS e bancos Amazon RDS nessas sub-redes gerenciadas centralmente sem obter permissões para alterar topologias de rede ou roteamento. Qual solução atende a esses requisitos com a MENOR complexidade operacional e custo?

options.text: Implantar um AWS Transit Gateway na conta Hub de Rede, provisionar VPCs individuais em cada uma das 120 contas-membro e criar anexos de VPC e associações de tabelas de rotas para cada conta.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Criar e manter 120 VPCs individuais multiplica a complexidade de gestão de blocos CIDR, custos de anexos de Transit Gateway (US$ 0,05/hora por anexo) e custos de infraestrutura redundante de NAT Gateways.

options.text: Configurar uma VPC centralizada multicamadas na conta Hub de Rede e usar o AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) para compartilhar as sub-redes privadas com toda a organização ou OUs específicas.
options.explanation: Correto: O VPC Sharing via AWS RAM permite que os administradores de rede centrais mantenham controle total sobre a infraestrutura de rede enquanto as contas-membro executam recursos de computação e banco de dados diretamente nas sub-redes compartilhadas.

options.text: Estabelecer conexões de VPC Peering em malha completa entre a VPC do Hub de Rede e as VPCs das 120 contas-membro, criando funções Lambda agendadas para sincronizar tabelas de rotas dinamicamente.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O VPC Peering exige VPCs separadas em cada conta, não permite compartilhar sub-redes diretamente e a sincronização customizada de rotas via Lambda introduz alto risco de falha operacional.

options.text: Implantar serviços de endpoint do AWS PrivateLink na conta Hub de Rede para cada componente de aplicação e criar Interface VPC Endpoints dentro de cada VPC de conta-membro de desenvolvimento.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O AWS PrivateLink foi projetado para expor endpoints de serviços TCP específicos, e não para compartilhar sub-redes genéricas onde aplicações precisam executar recursos arbitrários de computação e banco de dados.

pt.generalExplanation: O compartilhamento de VPC (VPC Sharing) via AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) permite que a conta central compartilhe sub-redes com contas-membro da organização, permitindo que desenvolvedores criem recursos diretamente sem gerenciar infraestrutura de rede.

es.domainName: Dominio 1: Diseñar Soluciones para la Complejidad Organizacional
es.statement: Un conglomerado tecnológico tiene 120 cuentas de desarrollo administradas bajo AWS Organizations en la misma Región de AWS. El equipo de redes exige que todas las subredes, tablas de rutas, asignaciones CIDR IPv4 y NAT Gateways salientes pertenezcan y sean administrados centralmente en una cuenta de Hub de Red dedicada. Sin embargo, los desarrolladores en las cuentas miembro deben poder desplegar instancias EC2, tareas ECS y bases RDS en estas subredes compartidas sin permisos para modificar topologías de red ni enrutamiento. ¿Qué solución cumple con estos requisitos con la MENOR complejidad operativa y costo?

options.text: Implementar un AWS Transit Gateway en la cuenta Hub de Red, aprovisionar VPCs individuales en cada una de las 120 cuentas miembro y crear adjuntos de VPC y asociaciones de tablas de rutas para cada cuenta.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Crear y administrar 120 VPCs individuales multiplica la complejidad de asignación de CIDR, las tarifas por adjunto de Transit Gateway y los costos redundantes de NAT Gateways.

options.text: Configurar una VPC multicapa centralizada en la cuenta Hub de Red y utilizar AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) para compartir las subredes privadas con toda la organización o OUs específicas.
options.explanation: Correcto: VPC Sharing a través de AWS RAM permite a los administradores de red centrales retener el control total de la infraestructura mientras las cuentas miembro lanzan recursos de cómputo y bases de datos directamente en subredes compartidas.

options.text: Establecer conexiones de VPC Peering en malla completa entre la VPC del Hub de Red y las VPCs de las 120 cuentas miembro, creando funciones Lambda programadas para sincronizar tablas de rutas.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: VPC Peering requiere VPCs separadas en cada cuenta, no permite compartir subredes directamente y la sincronización personalizada con Lambda introduce un alto riesgo operativo.

options.text: Implementar servicios de endpoint de AWS PrivateLink en la cuenta Hub de Red para cada componente y crear Interface VPC Endpoints dentro de la VPC de cada cuenta miembro de desarrollo.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: AWS PrivateLink está diseñado para exponer endpoints de servicios TCP específicos, no para compartir subredes genéricas donde las aplicaciones requieren desplegar recursos arbitrarios de cómputo.

es.generalExplanation: El uso compartido de VPC (VPC Sharing) mediante AWS RAM permite a la cuenta central compartir subredes con cuentas miembro de la organización, permitiendo a los desarrolladores lanzar recursos directamente sin administrar infraestructura de red.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A global banking institution requires dedicated, low-latency hybrid connectivity between its on-premises corporate data centers and 160 VPCs spread across 4 AWS Regions. The compliance framework mandates point-to-point Layer 2 hardware encryption (MACsec) across the physical interconnects, automated active/passive path failover over the AWS global backbone, and centralized BGP routing administration with minimal peering overhead. Which hybrid networking architecture should the lead architect deploy?

options.text: Provision dedicated 1 Gbps Direct Connect connections at two provider facilities, configure IPsec VPN tunnels with BGP over Private Virtual Interfaces (Private VIFs) attached directly to each of the 160 VPC Virtual Private Gateways.
options.explanation: Incorrect: 1 Gbps Direct Connect connections do not support MACsec (requires 10 Gbps or 100 Gbps dedicated ports), Private VIFs have a hard limit of 50 per connection, and creating 160 direct VIFs violates the minimal management requirement.

options.text: Deploy two 10 Gbps dedicated Direct Connect connections with MACsec enabled, provision 160 Public Virtual Interfaces (Public VIFs), and establish AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections over the Public VIFs to regional AWS Transit Gateways.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Running IPsec VPN tunnels over Public VIFs introduces encryption overhead and caps individual tunnel throughput at 1.25 Gbps, wasting the 10 Gbps dedicated line capacity and adding unnecessary routing complexity.

options.text: Deploy AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections across the public internet using Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN with AWS Global Accelerator, terminating tunnels on an AWS Network Load Balancer in each of the 4 AWS Regions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Public internet VPNs do not provide dedicated physical interconnects or Layer 2 MACsec hardware encryption and cannot terminate directly on Network Load Balancers.

options.text: Provision two dedicated 10 Gbps Direct Connect connections with MACsec enabled, configure a Direct Connect Gateway associated with regional AWS Transit Gateways via Transit VIFs in each AWS Region, and use BGP AS-Path prepending for path preference.
options.explanation: Correct: 10 Gbps dedicated Direct Connect ports support line-rate MACsec encryption. A Direct Connect Gateway associated with regional Transit Gateways scales to hundreds of VPCs across multiple regions with unified BGP management and seamless AS-Path failover.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying dedicated 10G/100G Direct Connect connections with MACsec enabled, associating a Direct Connect Gateway with regional Transit Gateways via Transit Virtual Interfaces (Transit VIFs), and configuring BGP AS-Path prepending fulfills all requirements with minimal BGP management overhead.

pt.statement: Uma instituição bancária global exige conectividade híbrida dedicada de baixa latência entre seus data centers corporativos on-premises e 160 VPCs distribuídas em 4 Regiões AWS. O framework de conformidade exige criptografia de hardware de Camada 2 ponto a ponto (MACsec) nos links físicos, failover automático de caminho ativo/passivo pelo backbone global da AWS e administração centralizada de roteamento BGP com sobrecarga mínima de gerenciamento de pares. Qual arquitetura de rede híbrida o arquiteto líder deve implantar?

options.text: Provisionar conexões dedicadas de 1 Gbps do Direct Connect em duas instalações de provedor, configurar túneis VPN IPsec com BGP sobre Private Virtual Interfaces (Private VIFs) anexadas diretamente aos 160 Virtual Private Gateways de cada VPC.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Portas de 1 Gbps do Direct Connect não suportam MACsec (exige portas dedicadas de 10 Gbps ou 100 Gbps), Private VIFs possuem limite rígido de 50 por conexão e criar 160 VIFs diretas viola a exigência de sobrecarga mínima de gestão.

options.text: Implantar duas conexões dedicadas de 10 Gbps do Direct Connect com MACsec ativado, provisionar 160 Public Virtual Interfaces (Public VIFs) e estabelecer conexões AWS Site-to-Site VPN sobre as Public VIFs para Transit Gateways regionais.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Executar túneis VPN IPsec sobre Public VIFs introduz sobrecarga computacional de criptografia e limita a taxa de transferência por túnel a 1,25 Gbps, subutilizando a capacidade dedicada de 10 Gbps e adicionando complexidade de roteamento.

options.text: Implantar conexões AWS Site-to-Site VPN pela internet pública usando Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN com AWS Global Accelerator, terminando os túneis em um AWS Network Load Balancer em cada uma das 4 Regiões AWS.
options.explanation: Incorreto: VPNs pela internet pública não fornecem interconexões físicas dedicadas nem criptografia de hardware MACsec de Camada 2, além de não poderem terminar diretamente em Network Load Balancers.

options.text: Provisionar duas conexões dedicadas de 10 Gbps do Direct Connect com MACsec ativado, configurar um Direct Connect Gateway associado a AWS Transit Gateways regionais via Transit VIFs em cada Região AWS e usar BGP AS-Path prepending para preferência de caminho.
options.explanation: Correto: Portas dedicadas de 10 Gbps do Direct Connect suportam criptografia MACsec na taxa de linha. O Direct Connect Gateway com Transit VIFs associado a Transit Gateways regionais escala para centenas de VPCs em múltiplas regiões com gestão unificada de BGP e failover por AS-Path.

pt.generalExplanation: A implantação de conexões dedicadas de 10G/100G do Direct Connect com MACsec ativado, associando um Direct Connect Gateway a Transit Gateways regionais via Transit VIFs e configurando BGP AS-Path prepending atende a todos os requisitos com mínima sobrecarga de gerenciamento BGP.

options.text: Implementar dos conexiones dedicadas de 10 Gbps de Direct Connect con MACsec habilitado, aprovisionar 160 Public VIFs y establecer conexiones AWS Site-to-Site VPN sobre las Public VIFs hacia Transit Gateways regionales.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Ejecutar túneles VPN IPsec sobre Public VIFs introduce sobrecarga y limita el rendimiento individual del túnel a 1.25 Gbps, desperdiciando la capacidad dedicada de 10 Gbps y agregando complejidad innecesaria.

options.text: Implementar conexiones AWS Site-to-Site VPN a través de internet pública utilizando Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN con AWS Global Accelerator, terminando los túneles en un AWS Network Load Balancer en cada región.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Las VPNs por internet pública no proporcionan interconexiones físicas dedicadas ni cifrado de hardware MACsec de Capa 2 y no pueden terminar directamente en Network Load Balancers.

options.explanation: Correcto: Los puertos dedicados de 10 Gbps de Direct Connect admiten cifrado MACsec a velocidad de línea. es.generalExplanation: Implementar conexiones dedicadas de Direct Connect de 10G/100G con MACsec habilitado, asociar un Direct Connect Gateway con Transit Gateways regionales mediante Transit VIFs y configurar BGP AS-Path prepending satisface todos los requisitos con mínima sobrecarga de gestión BGP.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A global healthcare enterprise is migrating 8,000 workforce identities from Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) to AWS Organizations managing 200 AWS accounts. The enterprise requires Single Sign-On (SSO) with Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and automated user lifecycle synchronization without replicating user passwords into AWS. Furthermore, data scientists and developers must be dynamically granted access to AWS resources (such as Amazon S3 buckets and Amazon SageMaker studio domains) based on their assigned corporate project department attribute, avoiding the creation and maintenance of hundreds of static IAM Permission Sets. Which combination of actions meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Deploy an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory in each of the 200 member accounts and establish two-way transitive forest trusts with the on-premises Microsoft Entra ID Domain Services.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Deploying AWS Managed AD in 200 individual accounts incurs enormous licensing costs, requires password synchronization, and introduces immense management overhead compared to centralized SSO federation.

options.text: Enable AWS IAM Identity Center in the AWS Organizations management account, configure SAML 2.0 identity federation with Microsoft Entra ID, and enable System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) automatic provisioning.
options.explanation: Correct: IAM Identity Center federates with Entra ID via SAML 2.0 for SSO/MFA without password synchronization, while SCIM automatically creates, updates, and deprovisions users and groups in real time.

options.text: Provision 200 separate IAM SAML Identity Providers and create dedicated IAM roles with hardcoded resource ARNs in every member account using AWS CloudFormation StackSets.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Managing separate SAML providers and static IAM roles across 200 accounts creates significant administrative burden and fails the requirement to avoid static project permission management.

options.text: Configure Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) in IAM Identity Center by passing the corporate Department attribute as an aws:PrincipalTag session tag, and attach an IAM policy using StringEquals condition on matching resource tags.
options.explanation: Correct: Passing user attributes as session tags in IAM Identity Center enables ABAC, allowing a single reusable Permission Set to grant granular access to any resource tagged with the corresponding Project/Department tag.

options.text: Create Amazon Cognito User Pools in each development account, synchronize directory users via AWS Lambda triggers, and generate temporary IAM STS credentials using Cognito Identity Pools.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon Cognito User Pools is designed for customer-facing consumer applications, not enterprise workforce SSO governance across multi-account AWS Organizations.

questions.generalExplanation: Integrating AWS IAM Identity Center with Microsoft Entra ID via SAML 2.0 and SCIM enables automated user provisioning and MFA without password replication. Configuring Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) using session tags (aws:PrincipalTag) in a single Permission Set enables dynamic access based on corporate project attributes.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Projetar Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Uma empresa global de saúde está migrando 8.000 identidades corporativas do Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) para o AWS Organizations, gerenciando 200 contas AWS. A empresa exige Single Sign-On (SSO) com Autenticação Multifator (MFA) e sincronização automatizada do ciclo de vida dos usuários sem replicar senhas no ambiente AWS. Além disso, cientistas de dados e desenvolvedores devem receber acesso dinâmico aos recursos da AWS (como buckets Amazon S3 e domínios Amazon SageMaker) com base no atributo de departamento de projeto corporativo atribuído, evitando a criação e manutenção de centenas de Permission Sets estáticos no IAM. Qual combinação de ações atende a esses requisitos? (Escolha duas.)

options.text: Implantar um diretório AWS Managed Microsoft AD em cada uma das 200 contas-membro e estabelecer relações de confiança de floresta transitivas bidirecionais com o Microsoft Entra ID Domain Services on-premises.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Implantar AWS Managed AD em 200 contas individuais gera custos de licenciamento astronômicos, exige sincronização de senhas e impõe complexidade extrema de manutenção quando comparado à federação centralizada com Identity Center.

options.text: Habilitar o AWS IAM Identity Center na conta de gerenciamento do AWS Organizations, configurar federação de identidade SAML 2.0 com o Microsoft Entra ID e ativar o provisionamento automático via SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management).
options.explanation: Correto: O IAM Identity Center federa com o Entra ID via SAML 2.0 para SSO e MFA sem sincronizar senhas, enquanto o protocolo SCIM sincroniza a criação, atualização e exclusão de usuários e grupos em tempo real.

options.text: Provisionar 200 provedores de identidade SAML do IAM separados e criar roles do IAM dedicadas com ARNs de recursos estáticos em cada conta-membro usando AWS CloudFormation StackSets.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Gerenciar provedores SAML e roles do IAM estáticas em 200 contas cria um fardo administrativo contínuo e viola o requisito de evitar a gestão estática de permissões por projeto.

options.text: Configurar Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) no IAM Identity Center repassando o atributo corporativo de Departamento como session tag aws:PrincipalTag e anexar uma política IAM com condição StringEquals correspondendo às tags dos recursos.
options.explanation: Correto: O repasse de atributos corporativos como session tags no IAM Identity Center viabiliza ABAC, permitindo que um único Permission Set reutilizável conceda acesso granular a qualquer recurso etiquetado com a tag de Projeto/Departamento correspondente.

options.text: Criar Amazon Cognito User Pools em cada conta de desenvolvimento, sincronizar usuários do diretório corporativo via triggers do AWS Lambda e gerar credenciais temporárias do IAM STS usando Cognito Identity Pools.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O Amazon Cognito foi desenvolvido para autenticação de clientes em aplicações web/mobile consumidoras (B2C), e não para governança de identidades corporativas de força de trabalho em ambientes multi-conta.

pt.generalExplanation: A integração do AWS IAM Identity Center com o Microsoft Entra ID via SAML 2.0 e SCIM permite provisionamento automatizado de usuários e MFA sem replicação de senhas. A configuração de Controle de Acesso Baseado em Atributos (ABAC) com session tags (aws:PrincipalTag) em um único Permission Set viabiliza acesso dinâmico baseado em atributos de projeto.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A corporate enterprise is restructuring its AWS footprint after acquiring a software subsidiary. The subsidiary operates 45 standalone AWS accounts within its legacy AWS Organization. A solutions architect must migrate all 45 member accounts from the legacy Organization into the primary corporate AWS Organization. All accounts have standalone payment methods and support contact information already configured. Which combination of steps must the architect execute to successfully transfer the member accounts? (Choose three.)

options.text: Call the MoveAccount API operation from the management account of the old organization, specifying the target Organizational Unit ID of the new corporate organization as the destination.
options.explanation: Incorrect: The MoveAccount API operation only moves an account between Organizational Units (OUs) within the same AWS Organization; it cannot move accounts across different organizations.

options.text: From the management account of the old organization, remove each subsidiary member account by calling the RemoveAccountFromOrganization API operation for all applicable account IDs.
options.explanation: Correct: Member accounts must first be released from their existing organization using RemoveAccountFromOrganization before they can join a new organization as independent standalone accounts.

options.text: Deploy an AWS CloudFormation StackSet from the new management account to provision cross-account IAM roles with AdministratorAccess in all subsidiary member accounts before removal.
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudFormation StackSets cannot deploy across different organizations without existing organizational trust, and cross-account roles do not perform the structural migration of account ownership.

options.text: Create temporary placeholder accounts in the new organization and call the MergeOrganizations API operation from the AWS CLI to merge organizational root hierarchies directly.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Organizations does not provide a MergeOrganizations API; organizations must be consolidated by migrating member accounts individually.

options.text: From the management account of the new corporate organization, send an invitation to each subsidiary account by calling the InviteAccountToOrganization API operation.
options.explanation: Correct: The target organization management account must initiate the onboarding process by issuing an invitation handshake via InviteAccountToOrganization.

options.text: Sign in to each individual subsidiary member account and accept the organizational invitation by calling the AcceptHandshake API operation with the appropriate handshake ID.
options.explanation: Correct: An authorized administrator within each invited member account must explicitly accept the invitation handshake using AcceptHandshake to finalize joining the new organization.

questions.generalExplanation: Migrating member accounts between AWS Organizations requires: (1) Removing each account from the old organization using RemoveAccountFromOrganization (called from the management account or member account), (2) Inviting each account from the new organization management account using InviteAccountToOrganization, and (3) Accepting the handshake/invitation from within each member account using AcceptHandshake.

options.text: From the management account of the new corporate organization, send an invitation to each subsidiary account by calling the InviteAccountToOrganization API operation.

en.generalExplanation: Migrating member accounts between AWS Organizations requires: (1) Removing each account from the old organization using RemoveAccountFromOrganization (called from the management account or member account), (2) Inviting each account from the new organization management account using InviteAccountToOrganization, and (3) Accepting the handshake/invitation from within each member account using AcceptHandshake.

options.text: Chamar a operação de API MoveAccount a partir da conta de gerenciamento da organização antiga, especificando o ID da Unidade Organizacional de destino da nova organização corporativa.
options.explanation: Incorreto: A operação de API MoveAccount serve exclusivamente para mover contas entre Unidades Organizacionais (OUs) dentro da mesma organização da AWS; ela não pode transferir contas entre organizações distintas.

options.text: A partir da conta de gerenciamento da organização antiga, remover cada conta-membro da subsidiária chamando a operação de API RemoveAccountFromOrganization para todos os IDs de conta aplicáveis.
options.explanation: Correto: As contas-membro devem primeiro ser desvinculadas da organização existente usando RemoveAccountFromOrganization antes que possam ingressar em uma nova organização como contas independentes.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: An enterprise uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled across 150 accounts. The central procurement team mandates that developers may only subscribe to third-party AMI and SaaS software products that have been pre-approved via an AWS Private Marketplace. Administrative rights to configure and approve Private Marketplace products must be restricted to a specific IAM role named procurement-admin-role located solely within the central Shared-Services account. All other IAM users, roles, and member account administrators must be strictly prohibited from modifying Private Marketplace configurations or assuming administrative roles. Which solution achieves this with the HIGHEST security and LEAST operational effort?

options.text: Create an IAM role named procurement-admin-role in every member account, attach the PowerUserAccess managed policy, and apply an inline policy to all other roles in all accounts that explicitly denies AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess.
options.explanation: Incorrect: PowerUserAccess does not manage Private Marketplace settings, and creating inline policies across thousands of IAM roles in 150 accounts creates massive operational overhead that can be bypassed by local account administrators.

options.text: Deploy an IAM Permissions Boundary to all developer IAM roles in all member accounts that permits only aws-marketplace:Subscribe actions on pre-approved product catalog ARNs.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Permissions Boundaries do not apply to account root users, cannot prevent administrators from modifying account-level marketplace settings, and require continuous maintenance during role provisioning.

options.text: Create the procurement-admin-role in the Shared-Services account with the AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess managed policy. Attach an organization-level SCP to the Root OU that explicitly denies Private Marketplace administrative actions to all principals except the procurement-admin-role, and attach a second SCP that denies creating an IAM role named procurement-admin-role across member accounts.
options.explanation: Correct: Combining a delegated procurement role in a central account with root-level SCPs prevents unauthorized marketplace configuration across all accounts while preventing member accounts from privilege-escalating by creating identical role names.

options.text: Enable AWS Control Tower in all accounts and configure detective guardrails using AWS Config managed rules to alert the security operations center whenever an unauthorized subscription occurs.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Config detective guardrails do not prevent developers from subscribing to unapproved software and require manual reactive revocation by security engineers.

questions.generalExplanation: Creating the procurement-admin-role in the Shared-Services account with the AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess managed policy and applying an organization-wide Root SCP that denies Private Marketplace administration actions to all principals except procurement-admin-role enforces centralized governance without per-account policy overhead.

Todos os outros usuários, roles do IAM e administradores de contas-membro devem ser estritamente proibidos de modificar configurações do Private Marketplace ou assumir roles administrativas. Qual solução alcança isso com a MAIOR segurança e MENOR esforço operacional?

options.text: Criar uma role do IAM chamada procurement-admin-role em todas as contas-membro, anexar a política gerenciada PowerUserAccess e aplicar uma política inline em todas as outras roles em todas as contas negando explicitamente AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess.
options.explanation: Incorreto: A política PowerUserAccess não concede privilégios administrativos no Private Marketplace, e gerenciar políticas inline em milhares de roles em 150 contas gera sobrecarga operacional massiva e pode ser contornado por administradores locais.

options.text: Implantar um IAM Permissions Boundary em todas as roles de desenvolvedores em todas as contas-membro permitindo apenas ações aws-marketplace:Subscribe em ARNs de catálogo de produtos aprovados.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Permissions Boundaries não afetam o usuário root das contas, não impedem que administradores locais alterem configurações organizacionais do marketplace e exigem manutenção contínua no provisionamento de roles.

options.explanation: Correto: A combinação de uma role de compras centralizada com SCPs na raiz da organização impede a configuração não autorizada do marketplace em todas as contas e previne elevação de privilégios impedindo a criação de roles com o mesmo nome nas contas-membro.

options.text: Habilitar o AWS Control Tower em todas as contas e configurar guardrails detectivos usando regras gerenciadas do AWS Config para alertar o centro de operações de segurança sempre que uma assinatura não autorizada ocorrer.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Guardrails detectivos do AWS Config não impedem que desenvolvedores assinem softwares não aprovados em tempo de execução, exigindo remediação manual reativa posterior.

es.generalExplanation: Crear el rol procurement-admin-role en la cuenta de Servicios Compartidos con la política administrada AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess y aplicar una SCP en la Raíz de la organización que deniegue acciones administrativas a todos los principales excepto a procurement-admin-role garantiza gobernanza centralizada sin sobrecarga de gestión.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A global media streaming platform captures telemetry and playback interaction events from over 10 million smart TVs and mobile apps simultaneously. The ingestion tier receives up to 150,000 JSON payloads per second. The architecture requires real-time sub-second ingestion, strictly ordered per-device event processing, automatic horizontal scaling without manual capacity intervention, and zero data loss during traffic spikes. Processed state must be stored in a globally replicated database with low read latency worldwide. Which serverless architecture satisfies these requirements with the HIGHEST resilience?

options.text: Ingest telemetry events through Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) Standard queues, trigger AWS Lambda functions with maximum concurrency to parse records, and write output documents into Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL with global read replicas.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon SQS Standard queues do not guarantee strict message ordering and SQS FIFO queues have throughput limits (up to 70,000 TPS with high throughput mode) that do not scale seamlessly to 150,000 TPS without complex sharding.

options.text: Ingest telemetry payloads into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams configured in On-Demand capacity mode using the device ID as the PartitionKey. Configure AWS Lambda as an event source mapping with a Parallelization Factor and BisectBatchOnFunctionError enabled, writing aggregate playback state into Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables.
options.explanation: Correct: Kinesis Data Streams On-Demand scales automatically up to gigabytes per second, preserves strict per-device ordering via PartitionKey, and Lambda with Parallelization Factor scales processing while DynamoDB Global Tables provides multi-region replication.

options.text: Publish telemetry events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) FIFO topic, route messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with an inline Lambda transformation, and stream transformed JSON files into Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
options.explanation: Incorrect: SNS FIFO topics have regional throughput quotas that cannot handle 150,000 TPS out of the box, and Firehose delivers micro-batches with latency (minimum 60 seconds) rather than sub-second real-time streaming.

options.text: Stream incoming events into an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) cluster with manual broker provisioning, and configure an Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS) Fargate service polling Kafka topics via consumer groups.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon MSK with manual broker provisioning requires ongoing operational overhead for broker capacity management and partition rebalancing, failing the serverless zero-maintenance requirement.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams in On-Demand mode paired with AWS Lambda event source mapping (with bisect-on-function-error and parallelization factor) and Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables provides scalable, strictly ordered per-partition key streaming with worldwide replication.

questions.statement: An autonomous vehicle research institution runs distributed deep learning model training jobs on clusters of hundreds of GPU-powered Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. Which storage architecture meets these extreme high-performance compute requirements?

options.text: Deploy an Amazon FSx for Lustre persistent file system with SSD storage, configured with an Amazon S3 data repository association (DRA) and automatic export data repository tasks.
options.explanation: Correct: FSx for Lustre Persistent SSD is specifically engineered for high-performance computing (HPC) and ML workloads, delivering sub-millisecond latencies, hundreds of GB/s throughput, POSIX compliance, and native bidirectional sync with Amazon S3.

options.text: Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system with General Purpose performance mode and Provisioned Throughput set to maximum capacity, mounting it across all EC2 instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: While Amazon EFS is POSIX compliant, its architecture is optimized for web serving and general enterprise shares rather than high-throughput parallel GPU training jobs requiring hundreds of GB/s.

options.text: Attach Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) io2 Block Express volumes configured with EBS Multi-Attach to all GPU instances simultaneously across all Availability Zones.
options.explanation: Incorrect: EBS Multi-Attach with io2 Block Express is restricted to instances within a single Availability Zone and requires a cluster-aware filesystem (e.g., GFS2) without offering native bidirectional synchronization with Amazon S3.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway instance in each Availability Zone backed by the training S3 bucket, mounting the resulting NFS shares on all EC2 training nodes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway is designed for hybrid on-premises to cloud backup and file tiering; it cannot deliver the sub-millisecond latency and hundreds of GB/s parallel throughput required for deep learning.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon FSx for Lustre Persistent deployment linked directly to an Amazon S3 data repository provides POSIX compatibility, massive parallel throughput (hundreds of GB/s), and seamless bidirectional data sync with S3.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A SaaS security provider hosts a multi-tenant analytics engine in an AWS VPC. More than 400 external enterprise customers need to securely connect their own AWS VPCs to the SaaS application over private AWS network infrastructure without exposing public IP addresses. Furthermore, all inbound customer traffic must be transparently routed through a scalable fleet of third-party intrusion detection and prevention system (IDS/IPS) virtual appliances without performing Source NAT (preserving client IP headers) or requiring overlapping IP range remediation. Which architecture meets these requirements with the LEAST operational complexity?

options.text: Establish bidirectional VPC Peering connections between the SaaS provider VPC and all 400 customer VPCs, and deploy open-source iptables firewall instances behind an Application Load Balancer in each customer account.
options.explanation: Incorrect: VPC Peering fails if any customer VPC has overlapping CIDR blocks with the SaaS VPC and cannot scale cleanly across 400 external accounts without routing table limits and massive management overhead.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Transit Gateway in the SaaS account, establish Transit Gateway VPC attachments to each customer VPC, and configure stateful EC2 proxy instances with Source NAT in the central VPC.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Transit Gateway requires cross-account attachments that do not support overlapping IP addresses natively without complex NAT, and Source NAT destroys original client IP visibility.

options.text: Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) with target groups pointing to the IDS/IPS appliances in a central inspection layer, placed inline in front of a Network Load Balancer (NLB) configured as an AWS PrivateLink Endpoint Service. Customers create Interface VPC Endpoints in their respective VPCs.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS PrivateLink enables private unidirectional access with complete isolation and zero IP overlap conflicts. Gateway Load Balancer uses GENEVE protocol (port 6081) to transparently inspect traffic while fully preserving original Layer 3/4 packet headers.

options.text: Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection from each customer VPC to an Amazon API Gateway Private REST API with mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication enabled on regional custom domains.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Site-to-Site VPN across 400 customer accounts introduces immense tunnel management complexity and API Gateway Private REST APIs do not support inline Layer 3/4 packet inspection via third-party IDS/IPS appliances.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS PrivateLink Endpoint Services backed by a Network Load Balancer enables private connectivity without overlapping CIDR issues, while AWS Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) transparently routes traffic to third-party virtual appliances using GENEVE encapsulation, preserving original client IP addresses.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A global industrial manufacturing enterprise is installing 500,000 smart energy meters across customer factories. During manufacturing, the company's private Certificate Authority (CA) flashes an X.509 device certificate onto each meter's hardware secure element, containing a unique serial number in the certificate Common Name. When meters are installed on-site and connect to the internet for the first time, they must securely authenticate to AWS IoT Core and be automatically provisioned with the appropriate IoT Thing name, certificate policy, and device shadow without manual pre-registration of each device by factory technicians. Which combination of steps must a solutions architect implement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Register the private root or intermediate Certificate Authority (CA) with AWS IoT Core, activate the CA certificate, and enable the allow-auto-registration flag on the registered CA.
options.explanation: Correct: Registering the private CA certificate in AWS IoT Core with auto-registration enabled allows devices signed by this CA to automatically initiate registration upon their first connection attempt.

options.text: Create a claim certificate in AWS IoT Core and embed the same shared private key and claim certificate on all 500,000 meters during the manufacturing phase.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Sharing a single claim certificate and private key across half a million devices violates the security principle of per-device unique cryptographic identity and creates massive vulnerability if one device is compromised.

options.text: Create an AWS IoT Core fleet provisioning template with a pre-provisioning AWS Lambda hook that validates the meter serial number from the certificate Common Name and attaches the appropriate IoT policy and device shadow dynamically.
options.explanation: Correct: A fleet provisioning template paired with a pre-provisioning Lambda hook executes custom validation logic (such as checking serial numbers) and automatically attaches least-privilege IoT policies and creates the Thing representation.

options.text: Configure Amazon Cognito Identity Pools with unauthenticated guest access to exchange device serial numbers for temporary AWS IAM STS credentials via the AWS CLI.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Using unauthenticated Cognito Identity Pools to hand out IAM credentials directly to public hardware devices is an egregious security anti-pattern.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Step Functions state machine triggered by AWS CloudTrail whenever a device connects to call the RegisterThing API operation synchronously.
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudTrail logs API events with latency of 5 to 15 minutes and does not trigger synchronously on MQTT TLS connection handshakes in AWS IoT Core.

questions.generalExplanation: Implementing Just-in-Time Registration (JITR) or Just-in-Time Provisioning (JITP) with a custom CA in AWS IoT Core involves registering the root/intermediate CA with allow-auto-registration enabled and configuring a pre-provisioning AWS Lambda hook to validate serial numbers and dynamically attach IoT policies and create device things.

pt.domainName: Domínio 2: Projetar Novas Soluções
pt.statement: Uma indústria de manufatura global está instalando 500.000 medidores de energia inteligentes em fábricas de clientes. Durante a fabricação, a Autoridade de Certificação (CA) privada da empresa grava um certificado de dispositivo X.509 no elemento seguro de hardware de cada medidor, contendo um número de série exclusivo no Common Name do certificado. Quando os medidores são instalados em campo e conectados à internet pela primeira vez, eles devem se autenticar com segurança no AWS IoT Core e ser provisionados automaticamente com o nome de IoT Thing apropriado, política de certificado e device shadow sem o pré-registro manual de cada dispositivo por técnicos em fábrica. Qual combinação de etapas um arquiteto de soluções deve implementar? (Escolha duas.)

options.text: Registrar a Autoridade de Certificação (CA) privada raiz ou intermediária no AWS IoT Core, ativar o certificado da CA e habilitar o parâmetro allow-auto-registration na CA registrada.
options.explanation: Correto: O registro do certificado da CA privada no AWS IoT Core com auto-registro habilitado permite que dispositivos assinados por essa CA iniciem automaticamente o processo de registro em sua primeira tentativa de conexão.

options.text: Criar um certificado de reivindicação (claim certificate) no AWS IoT Core e embutir a mesma chave privada compartilhada e certificado de reivindicação em todos os 500.000 medidores durante a fabricação.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Compartilhar um único certificado de reivindicação e chave privada em meio milhão de dispositivos viola o princípio de segurança de identidade criptográfica exclusiva por dispositivo e cria vulnerabilidade massiva se um aparelho for violado.

options.text: Criar um modelo de provisionamento de frota do AWS IoT Core com um gancho de pré-provisionamento do AWS Lambda que valida o número de série do medidor a partir do Common Name do certificado e anexa a política do IoT e o device shadow dinamicamente.
options.explanation: Correto: Um modelo de provisionamento de frota associado a um hook Lambda de pré-provisionamento executa validações personalizadas (como checagem de números de série) e anexa automaticamente políticas de menor privilégio e device shadows.

options.text: Configurar Amazon Cognito Identity Pools com acesso de convidado não autenticado para trocar números de série de dispositivos por credenciais temporárias do AWS IAM STS via AWS CLI.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Utilizar Cognito Identity Pools com acesso não autenticado para distribuir credenciais do IAM diretamente a dispositivos de hardware em campo é um grave anti-padrão de segurança.

options.text: Implantar uma máquina de estados do AWS Step Functions acionada pelo AWS CloudTrail sempre que um dispositivo se conecta para chamar a operação de API RegisterThing de forma síncrona.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O CloudTrail registra eventos de API com latência de 5 a 15 minutos e não é acionado de forma síncrona durante o handshake de conexão MQTT TLS no AWS IoT Core.

pt.generalExplanation: A implementação de Just-in-Time Registration (JITR) ou Just-in-Time Provisioning (JITP) com CA personalizada no AWS IoT Core envolve registrar a CA privada com allow-auto-registration ativado e configurar uma função AWS Lambda de pré-provisionamento para validar o número de série, anexar políticas do IoT e criar o objeto (thing) dinamicamente.

options.explanation: Correcto: Una plantilla de aprovisionamiento de flota con un hook de Lambda de pre-aprovisionamiento ejecuta lógica de validación personalizada y adjunta automáticamente políticas de IoT y shadows de menor privilegio.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A global logistics company processes high-volume freight shipping manifests submitted as large CSV datasets containing up to 2 million records each. When a manifest is uploaded to Amazon S3, an automated pipeline must process each record independently through multiple validation, geocoding, and customs calculation steps. The solution must support processing over 10,000 concurrent records without exceeding downstream API rate limits, ensure automated retries with exponential backoff, route poison pill records to a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) for manual inspection without halting the batch, and minimize custom orchestration code. Which architecture satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Configure an Amazon S3 event notification to invoke a single AWS Lambda function that parses the entire 2 million record CSV file in memory and spawns multithreaded worker processes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Lambda has a 15-minute maximum execution timeout and memory limits (10 GB) that will fail when parsing and orchestrating 2 million records with external API calls in a single function invocation.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon EMR cluster with Apache Spark on EC2 On-Demand instances, writing custom Python scripts to split the CSV, handle retries, and write failed records into an Amazon DynamoDB error table.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Managing a persistent EMR cluster requires substantial operational overhead and custom Spark retry code compared to native managed serverless step orchestrators.

options.text: Configure S3 event notifications to publish messages directly to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) topic that fans out to 1,000 independent AWS Lambda functions without concurrency controls.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Fanning out directly from SNS to thousands of concurrent Lambdas lacks concurrency throttling controls and will overwhelm downstream geocoding and customs APIs with rate-limit errors.

options.text: Use Amazon EventBridge to trigger an AWS Step Functions state machine configured with a Distributed Map state in ItemReader mode directly reading the S3 CSV object. Configure maxConcurrency to protect downstream APIs, define built-in retry and Catch blocks, and send failed items to an Amazon SQS Dead-Letter Queue.
options.explanation: Correct: Step Functions Distributed Map natively streams and splits large datasets (up to millions of items) from Amazon S3, executes parallel child workflows with concurrency control (maxConcurrency), and handles retries and DLQs natively without custom glue code.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon EventBridge triggering AWS Step Functions in Distributed Map mode with S3 object source, custom concurrency limits, built-in error handling with retry policies, and an Amazon SQS DLQ fulfills large-scale batch processing with minimal code.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A healthcare analytics organization exchanges sensitive patient clinical trial records with external laboratory partners using SFTP. Partners upload files encrypted using Pretty Good Privacy (PGP) to an AWS Transfer Family SFTP server backed by Amazon S3. The security architecture requires an automated serverless workflow that automatically decrypts incoming PGP files upon successful upload and saves the unencrypted files into a target S3 bucket for downstream analytics. The solution must securely retrieve the decryption key and handle processing without provisioning custom EC2 instances or maintaining long-running daemon servers. Which solution satisfies these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Store the PGP public key in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure an S3 event notification on the landing bucket to trigger an AWS Lambda function that downloads the file, calls GnuPG via a custom container layer, and uploads the decrypted output.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Decrypting files requires the PGP private key (not the public key), and building custom Lambda layers with GnuPG requires ongoing code and runtime maintenance compared to managed native Transfer Family workflows.

options.text: Store the PGP private key in AWS Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Transfer Family managed workflow with a nominal step configured for PGP decryption referencing the Secrets Manager secret ARN, and attach the workflow to the Transfer Family server or SFTP user.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Transfer Family provides native managed workflows with built-in PGP decryption steps that integrate directly with AWS Secrets Manager to retrieve the private key securely without writing any custom code.

options.text: Store the PGP public key in AWS Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Transfer Family managed workflow with an exception-handling step configured for PGP encryption referencing the Secrets Manager secret ARN, and attach the workflow to the S3 bucket policy.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Exception handling steps only run when a prior step fails, public keys are for encryption rather than decryption, and Transfer Family workflows cannot be attached to S3 bucket policies.

options.text: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance running a cron daemon that mounts the Amazon S3 bucket using S3FS-FUSE, periodically scans for new .pgp files, decrypts them using local GPG keys, and moves them to the target S3 prefix.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Running custom EC2 cron instances with FUSE mounts introduces single points of failure, scaling bottlenecks, security key exposure risks on disk, and high operational management overhead.

questions.generalExplanation: Storing the PGP private key in AWS Secrets Manager and attaching an AWS Transfer Family managed workflow with a built-in PGP decryption step configured with the Secrets Manager ARN to the SFTP server executes automated decryption natively upon file arrival.

questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: An enterprise operates an e-commerce platform across 40 VPCs in the us-east-1 Region. Application workloads running on private Amazon EC2 instances and ECS tasks generate petabytes of monthly traffic transferring product images and catalog assets to Amazon S3 buckets and performing millions of read/write queries against Amazon DynamoDB tables. Financial analysis reveals that NAT Gateway data processing fees ($0.045 per GB) account for over 45% of total AWS networking costs. Which combination of networking enhancements will reduce data transfer and processing costs to the LOWEST possible amount without disrupting connectivity? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create Gateway VPC Endpoints for Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB in every application VPC route table pointing to the respective service prefix lists.
options.explanation: Correct: Gateway VPC Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are completely free of charge (no hourly fee and no data processing fee), instantly bypassing NAT Gateways and eliminating all data transfer costs for those services.

options.text: Deploy Interface VPC Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) for Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB across two private subnets in all 40 application VPCs.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Interface VPC Endpoints incur both an hourly fee per Availability Zone ($0.01/hr) and data processing charges ($0.01/GB), which is significantly more expensive than completely free Gateway Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB.

options.text: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on all customer-facing S3 buckets and configure EC2 instances to download images using Accelerated bucket endpoints.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Transfer Acceleration is designed for public internet transfers from distant geographical regions and incurs additional data transfer fees ($0.04 to $0.08 per GB), dramatically increasing costs for in-region transfers.

options.text: Replace all private subnets in the application VPCs with public subnets, assign Elastic IP addresses to all EC2 instances, and eliminate NAT Gateways entirely.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Exposing internal application servers and databases in public subnets with direct internet routability introduces critical security compliance violations and security exposure.

options.text: Consolidate non-S3/DynamoDB internet egress traffic by routing spoke VPC 0.0.0.0/0 traffic through a centralized Egress VPC containing shared NAT Gateways attached via an AWS Transit Gateway.
options.explanation: Correct: Consolidating internet egress traffic through centralized NAT Gateways in a shared services VPC eliminates the hourly base provisioning costs of running redundant NAT Gateways across 40 individual VPCs.

questions.generalExplanation: Creating Gateway VPC Endpoints for Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB routes traffic directly across the AWS private network at zero cost per GB and zero hourly fee. questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: An online ticketing platform experiences rapid, unpredictable 10x traffic surges when high-profile concerts and sporting events go on sale. The platform runs on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). During past sales, users encountered HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout errors because EC2 Auto Scaling groups based on average CPU utilization scaled out too slowly to provision new underlying compute capacity before tasks became overloaded. The solution must provide sub-minute task scaling, optimize EC2 compute costs during baseline hours, and automatically scale underlying EC2 infrastructure in step with task placement demands. Which architecture satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Configure an ECS service on AWS Fargate with a scheduled scaling policy that increases task count to maximum limits 24 hours prior to expected ticket sales, keeping tasks running continuously.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Scheduled scaling requires knowing the exact date and time of all surges in advance and running maximum Fargate capacity for 24 hours results in excessive, unnecessary compute expenses.

options.text: Create a single EC2 Auto Scaling group of On-Demand instances configured with simple scaling policies based on NetworkIn CloudWatch alarms with a 10-minute cooldown period.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Simple scaling with 10-minute cooldowns reacts too slowly to sudden traffic spikes, and NetworkIn metrics do not accurately reflect web request processing concurrency.

options.text: Configure ECS Capacity Providers with Managed Scaling and Managed Termination Protection, backed by an Auto Scaling group using a mixed instances policy with Spot and On-Demand instances. Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling using target tracking based on the Application Load Balancer RequestCountPerTarget metric.
options.explanation: Correct: ECS Capacity Providers use the CapacityProviderReservation metric to automatically scale the underlying EC2 cluster in lockstep with pending ECS tasks, while target tracking on ALB RequestCountPerTarget scales task count dynamically before CPU saturation occurs.

options.text: Provision static EC2 Metal instances in a spread placement group, configure a cron job to launch new Docker containers via SSH, and disable AWS Auto Scaling.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Using static metal instances with manual SSH scripts is an unscalable, highly complex operational anti-pattern that fails cost and automation requirements.

questions.generalExplanation: Configuring ECS Capacity Providers with managed scaling and managed instance protection, using a mixed-instance Auto Scaling group with EC2 Spot and On-Demand instances, and setting ALB target tracking on RequestCountPerTarget enables responsive and cost-effective scaling.

questions.statement: A multinational enterprise manages 220 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. Corporate cybersecurity compliance mandates that all application logs, operating system audit logs, and VPC Flow Logs generated in member accounts must be continuously streamed to a centralized Security Account in real time. In the Security Account, logs must be ingested into an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster for 30-day interactive analysis and simultaneously stored in an encrypted Amazon S3 data lake bucket with immutable storage for 7-year regulatory compliance. The solution must support automated cross-account ingestion with minimal per-account infrastructure overhead. Which architecture meets these requirements?

options.text: Install Amazon OpenSearch Service Logstash agents on every EC2 instance and container in all 220 member accounts, configuring agents to output logs directly over public HTTPS endpoints to the central OpenSearch cluster.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Installing and maintaining third-party agents on thousands of instances across 220 accounts creates massive operational maintenance and exposes ingestion endpoints to the public internet.

options.text: Create AWS Lambda functions in every member account triggered by CloudWatch Logs to read log batches, format JSON payloads, and call the OpenSearch Index API and S3 PutObject API across accounts synchronously.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Custom Lambda functions in 220 accounts incur high execution costs, introduce throttling risks under log volume surges, and require custom error handling and retry mechanisms.

options.text: Configure VPC Flow Logs and application logs to write directly to Amazon S3 buckets in each member account, and use AWS DataSync scheduled hourly tasks to replicate logs to the central Security Account.
options.explanation: Incorrect: DataSync hourly sync introduces a 1-hour delay, failing the real-time streaming mandate, and requires managing 220 separate S3 buckets and sync tasks.

options.text: Create a centralized Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream in the Security Account configured with destinations to Amazon OpenSearch Service and the compliance S3 bucket. Create a CloudWatch Logs cross-account Destination in the Security Account, and deploy CloudWatch Logs Subscription Filters across all member accounts pointing to the central Destination.
options.explanation: Correct: CloudWatch Logs Subscription Filters natively stream log events cross-account into a Kinesis Data Firehose stream in the Security Account, which automatically buffers, formats, and delivers logs to OpenSearch for searching and S3 for compliance storage.

questions.generalExplanation: Configuring CloudWatch Logs Subscription Filters in member accounts using cross-account destination permissions pointing to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose stream in the Security Account delivers logs simultaneously to Amazon OpenSearch Service and Amazon S3 with zero per-account proxy infrastructure.
