questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: A healthcare provider stores 8 PB of patient medical scan images in an Amazon S3 bucket. Access patterns dictate that scans are frequently retrieved during the first 30 days after upload, rarely accessed between 31 and 365 days, and accessed once every few years thereafter for legal audits. SEC and HIPAA regulations mandate that all images must remain strictly immutable (WORM - Write Once Read Many) for 7 years, ensuring that neither standard IAM principals nor the AWS account root user can delete or overwrite objects during the retention period. Which storage architecture meets these requirements with the LOWEST cost and HIGHEST compliance?

options.text: Enable S3 Versioning, configure S3 Lifecycle to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days, and apply an S3 Bucket Policy with an explicit Deny on s3:DeleteObject for all IAM principals.
options.explanation: Incorrect: IAM Bucket Policies can be modified or deleted by the account root user or administrators with s3:PutBucketPolicy permissions, failing the regulatory requirement for non-bypassable WORM compliance.

options.text: Enable S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode with a default 7-year retention period on the bucket. Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 30 days and to S3 Glacier Flexible Archive after 365 days.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode cannot be overridden or deleted by any user (including the AWS root account) until the retention duration expires. S3 Intelligent-Tiering and Glacier Flexible Archive minimize storage costs for unpredictable long-term archive access.

options.text: Enable S3 Object Lock in Governance Mode with a 7-year retention period, and configure S3 Lifecycle to transition objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access after 30 days.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Governance Mode allows users with s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permissions to delete objects, violating the strict compliance mandate, and S3 One Zone-IA lacks multi-AZ resilience for medical records.

options.text: Deploy an AWS KMS customer managed key (CMK) with automatic annual key rotation and configure an AWS Backup vault lock with a 7-year retention policy applied to daily EBS snapshots.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Medical images are stored in Amazon S3, not on EBS block volumes, and KMS key rotation does not prevent S3 object deletion.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 Lifecycle transitions objects from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering and then to S3 Glacier Flexible Archive, while S3 Object Lock configured in Compliance Mode prevents all users (including root) from deleting objects until the retention period expires.

options.text: Deploy an AWS CloudFormation StackSet that configures Amazon Inspector to scan EC2 instances daily and trigger AWS Lambda functions in the root management account to terminate instances with open ports.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A legacy insurance enterprise plans to lift-and-shift 800 VMware virtual machines from an on-premises data center to Amazon EC2. The business requires minimal disruption during migration, continuous block-level data replication over an existing 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection, non-disruptive automated testing of target EC2 instances prior to final cutover, and a maintenance cutover window of less than 15 minutes per server wave. Which migration strategy satisfies these operational requirements with the LEAST cutover downtime?

options.text: Export all 800 VMware virtual machines as VMDK files, upload the VMDKs to Amazon S3 buckets using AWS DataSync, and call the VM Import/Export CLI command to generate EC2 AMIs.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Exporting and uploading multi-terabyte VMDK images is a slow, offline process that requires shutting down source VMs or taking static snapshots, causing extensive downtime and exceeding the 15-minute cutover window.

options.text: Install the AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) Replication Agent on all on-premises source virtual machines to perform continuous, block-level data replication over the Direct Connect connection. Perform non-disruptive launch test instances in AWS to validate applications, and initiate final cutover during the scheduled maintenance window.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) provides continuous asynchronous block-level replication, allows testing target instances in isolated subnets without stopping replication, and executes final server cutover in minutes with negligible downtime.

options.text: Deploy AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) connector in the vCenter environment to create daily incremental AMI snapshots, and execute manual CloudFormation scripts during the cutover window.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) is legacy and snapshot-based (creating replication lag between snapshots), whereas AWS MGN is the modern AWS standard providing continuous real-time block-level replication.

options.text: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate virtual machine operating system disks directly to Amazon EBS gp3 volumes attached to placeholder EC2 instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) is designed for database and analytical data store migrations; it cannot replicate operating systems, system state, or bootable virtual machines.

questions.generalExplanation: Installing the AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) agent on on-premises virtual machines enables continuous, non-disruptive block-level data replication over Direct Connect, supports automated launch of test instances without interrupting replication, and executes final cutover within minutes.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A retail banking enterprise is migrating its core 15 TB on-premises Oracle database containing stored procedures, custom PL/SQL packages, and complex relational schemas to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The business requires continuous transactional operation on the on-premises database throughout the migration lifecycle, zero data loss, schema and code compatibility validation prior to cutover, and a final database cutover window of less than 10 minutes. Which combination of tools and steps should the lead database architect implement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Export all Oracle tables using Oracle Data Pump (expdp) into flat CSV files, transfer them using AWS Snowball Edge, and import data into Aurora PostgreSQL using the pg_restore command.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Oracle Data Pump to Snowball requires taking offline exports or introduces static data lag that cannot capture real-time transactions occurring during the multi-day physical device shipping process.

options.text: Deploy AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) to perform block-level replication of the Oracle database server storage directly into the Aurora PostgreSQL shared storage volume.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS MGN is a block-level server migration tool for identical operating systems and disk volumes; it cannot perform heterogeneous schema conversion from Oracle database engine to PostgreSQL engine.

options.text: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to analyze database objects, generate a migration assessment report, and automatically convert Oracle schema, stored procedures, functions, and triggers to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL dialect.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS SCT is specifically built for heterogeneous database migrations, automating the conversion of Oracle relational schemas, data types, and PL/SQL code to PostgreSQL-compatible PL/pgSQL.

options.text: Configure Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL as an Oracle Data Guard physical standby database, establishing synchronous redo transport over AWS Direct Connect.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Oracle Data Guard is a proprietary Oracle disaster recovery feature that operates strictly between identical Oracle database instances; it cannot replicate to PostgreSQL engines.

options.text: Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance and configure a migration task with Full Load plus Change Data Capture (CDC) with validation enabled to continuously replicate ongoing changes until cutover.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS DMS with CDC continuously captures live Oracle transactional redo changes and applies them in real time to Aurora PostgreSQL, allowing business operations to continue on-premises until the final low-downtime cutover.

questions.generalExplanation: Using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to assess schema compatibility and convert Oracle PL/SQL stored procedures and triggers to PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL, combined with AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) configured for full load plus ongoing Change Data Capture (CDC), enables near-zero downtime migration.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: An enterprise runs a monolithic legacy enterprise resource planning (ERP) system hosted on on-premises virtual machines. options.text: Deploy an AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces environment spanning the legacy network account and new microservices accounts. options.explanation: Correct: AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces is purpose-built to accelerate the Strangler Fig pattern across multiple AWS accounts, automatically provisioning and orchestrating API Gateway, Transit Gateway, and private Network Load Balancers to route traffic incrementally.

options.text: Configure an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy configured to send 10% of DNS queries to the new microservices ALB and 90% to the on-premises legacy server IP addresses.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Route 53 weighted DNS routing distributes all traffic randomly based on IP resolution, which routes entire sessions to incomplete backends rather than routing specific API paths (/orders vs /inventory) deterministically.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Lambda@Edge function associated with an Amazon CloudFront distribution, hardcoding HTTP rewrite rules in Node.js to route requests across private VPC Peering connections.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Lambda@Edge cannot communicate directly with private IP addresses inside private VPCs or on-premises networks over VPC Peering without complex public proxies.

options.text: Deploy an open-source NGINX reverse proxy cluster on Amazon EC2 instances in each development account and write custom cron scripts to synchronize routing configuration files across servers.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed NGINX proxy fleets create single points of failure, require ongoing patching and configuration maintenance, and do not provide automated cross-account routing orchestration.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces orchestrates API Gateway, Network Load Balancer, and Transit Gateway across multiple AWS accounts to transparently route traffic between legacy on-premises applications and modern microservices using the Strangler Fig pattern.

A solução deve gerenciar o roteamento de rede híbrida e entre VPCs de forma transparente, isolar ambientes de desenvolvimento em múltiplas contas AWS e fornecer controle unificado de roteamento sem exigir alterações no código do sistema legado. options.explanation: Correto: O AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces foi desenvolvido especificamente para acelerar a refatoração pelo padrão Strangler Fig em múltiplas contas AWS, provisionando e orquestrando automaticamente API Gateway, Transit Gateway e Network Load Balancers para redirecionar tráfego progressivamente.

questions.statement: An enterprise is migrating 3 PB of unstructured engineering design data from on-premises NetApp SAN/NAS storage arrays to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP over an AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection. The file system contains hundreds of millions of files with complex POSIX and SMB NTFS permissions, hard links, symlinks, extended attributes, and ownership metadata. The migration must execute automated incremental synchronizations during business hours with bandwidth limits to prevent saturating production traffic, guarantee file metadata fidelity upon cutover, and minimize custom synchronization scripts. Which migration architecture should the solutions architect deploy?

options.text: Order 35 AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices, manually copy files using the Snowball Client, physically ship the devices to AWS, and import data directly into an Amazon S3 Standard bucket.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Snowball Edge devices take weeks to ship back and forth, do not support incremental live synchronization before cutover, and importing into S3 does not preserve native NetApp ONTAP filesystem structures directly.

options.text: Deploy an EC2 instance running rsync over an IPsec VPN tunnel connected to the on-premises NAS, executing a shell script that transfers files to Amazon Elastic File System (EFS).
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard single-threaded rsync over VPN is extremely slow for hundreds of millions of files across 3 PB, fails to preserve Windows SMB NTFS permissions accurately, and targets EFS instead of the required FSx for ONTAP.

options.text: Use the S3 File Gateway of AWS Storage Gateway deployed as a virtual appliance in vSphere, copying data to an S3 bucket and triggering Lambda functions to convert files into FSx volumes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 File Gateway is designed for hybrid file-to-object tiering; it does not perform automated multi-threaded parallel replication to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with metadata fidelity.

options.text: Deploy AWS DataSync agents in the on-premises VMware environment. Create an AWS DataSync task targeting the on-premises NFS/SMB shares as the source location and the Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system as the destination location, configuring bandwidth throttling schedules and full metadata preservation verification.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS DataSync uses a purpose-built network protocol to parallelize data transfers up to 10 Gbps, natively preserves all POSIX/SMB permissions, timestamps, and extended attributes, and provides automated task scheduling with bandwidth throttling during business hours.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A global financial corporation operates an IBM z/OS mainframe executing critical nightly batch processing jobs written in COBOL against VSAM files and DB2 databases. The enterprise is modernizing this workload to the AWS Cloud to eliminate multimillion-dollar mainframe licensing costs while enabling modern SQL-based analytics on historical transactions. The target architecture must support running re-platformed COBOL batch applications with high reliability, automated job scheduling, and transformed analytics storage utilizing an open-table format (Apache Iceberg) on Amazon S3 with sub-minute query response times in Amazon Athena. Which modernized architecture should the enterprise deploy?

options.text: Emulate the mainframe architecture by launching an Amazon EC2 Mac instance, installing a custom open-source COBOL compiler, and writing output records to local EBS volumes queried via SQLite.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Running custom emulators on EC2 Mac instances lacks enterprise support, job scheduling reliability, horizontal scalability, and integration with modern distributed cloud data lakes.

options.text: Rewrite all COBOL batch business logic into AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda functions within 30 days, storing all transaction history in Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Streams enabled.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Completely rewriting millions of lines of complex COBOL business logic in 30 days is exceptionally high-risk and impractical, and DynamoDB is not optimized for ad-hoc analytical SQL scans.

options.text: Deploy the COBOL batch applications using AWS Mainframe Modernization service with the Micro Focus (replatform) managed runtime environment. Ingest batch output files using AWS Glue ETL jobs that transform data into Apache Iceberg table format registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog on Amazon S3, and query transactional datasets using Amazon Athena.
